title: Generic freeness for finitely presented algebra-module pairs
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative integral domain and $A$ a commutative $R$-algebra admitting a presentation $A\cong R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ for finite $n,m\geq0$. Let $L$ be a finitely presented $A$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. There is $0\ne a\in R$ such that $L_a$ is a free $R_a$-module, where $R_a=R[1/a]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] and $L_a$ is the localized module [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] of fractions $\ell/a^j$ with equality $\ell/a^j=\ell'/a^k$ if and only if some power of $a$ annihilates $a^k\ell-a^j\ell'$. Free means isomorphic to $\bigoplus_{i\in I}R_a$ for some set $I$, which need not be finite. No Noetherian hypothesis on $R$ is imposed.

proof.text: Shrink the finite-type R-algebra A to Type u using Algebra.FiniteType.small and Shrink.algEquiv. Transport finite presentation and the action on L. Apply lem-weil-pbc-limit-module-finite-presentation and choose any stage: it gives S finite type over Z, B finite type over S, a finite B-module N, and an R-linear equivalence R tensor_S N ≃ L. Its stated R-action on L is the composite through A; IsScalarTower.algebraMap_smul identifies it with the given action. The finite-type permanence theorem makes S Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 051S, proof, with finite-presentation approximation Tag 00R1

proof.text: Let S₀ be the image subring of S → R. The surjection S → S₀ makes S₀ Noetherian, and the inclusion S₀ ⊆ R makes it a domain. Define B₀ = S₀ tensor_S B and N₀ = B₀ tensor_B N. Base change preserves finite type and finite generation. The tensor pushout cancellation equivalence identifies N₀ with S₀ tensor_S N; a second tensor cancellation identifies R tensor_{S₀} N₀ with L. No flatness of S → S₀ or S₀ → R is used.

source.place: Tag 051S, proof, with finite-presentation approximation Tag 00R1

proof.text: Apply lem-pur-noetherian-algebra-module-generic-freeness to the Noetherian domain S₀, the finite-type algebra B₀ and the finite B₀-module N₀. Obtain a nonzero a in S₀ for which (N₀)_a is free over (S₀)_a. Its image in R is nonzero by injectivity of the subring inclusion.

source.place: Tag 051S, proof, with finite-presentation approximation Tag 00R1

proof.text: Put T = R_a and U = (S₀)_a. The universal property of ring localization gives U → T. Identify (N₀)_a with U tensor_{S₀} N₀ using LocalizedModule.equivTensorProduct. IsBaseChange.free gives freeness of T tensor_U (U tensor_{S₀} N₀). Tensor cancellation identifies this with T tensor_{S₀} N₀, then with T tensor_R (R tensor_{S₀} N₀), then with T tensor_R L and finally L_a. These are linear equivalences over T; transport freeness through them. This works also for the zero module and for infinite basis index sets.
